name: subtitle
text: Why the synthetic tail is no longer an insertion problem, and why escape remains the live question.
textPreview: Why the synthetic tail is no longer an insertion problem, and why escape remains the live question.

text:
Open with the distinction. We used to phrase the problem as 'we do not find the minor conformer.' The newer evidence says the minor density is often already in the model, but in the wrong configuration. That changes the mechanism we should test.

name: cascade-callout
text: Rotamer, clash, and symmetry remove only 4 starts after occupancy; tmol is the dominant remaining filter.
textPreview: Rotamer, clash, and symmetry remove only 4 starts after occupancy; tmol is the dominant remaining filter.

text:

name: nulls-panel-copy
text: The failed arms mostly changed scoring or local search. None cleanly tested escape from a rewarded partial fit.
textPreview: The failed arms mostly changed scoring or local search. None cleanly tested escape from a rewarded partial fit.

text:
Do not narrate this as a graveyard of attempts. The pattern is the argument. Initialization is the sharpest null: even slots initialized on the minor moved away, so the issue was not simply lack of initial coverage.

name: gd
text: Gradient descent will not break a fit it is currently rewarded for making.
textPreview: Gradient descent will not break a fit it is currently rewarded for making.

name: sde
text: Noise or restart can test escape; insertion cannot.
textPreview: Noise or restart can test escape; insertion cannot.

text:
This is the movable-point argument. The wrong configuration explains real density at about 66 percent efficiency, so the objective rewards it locally. Gradient descent will not first break that partial fit in order to find a better one.

textPreview: - S2 looks like non-convergence, not a clean failed-escape result

name: bullet-1
text: - The honest test is smaller perturbation around local minima
textPreview: - The honest test is smaller perturbation around local minima

name: bullet-2
text: - Decision: spend another quarter on S1 or move to experimental density
textPreview: - Decision: spend another quarter on S1 or move to experimental density

text:
Frame this as the question for Fraser. S2 at 30 degrees per step was too much: it damaged convergence and worsened both missed-minor and missed-major categories. That does not refute escape. S1 at 10 degrees is the clean version of the question.
